allowed_evidence: line-addressable cuneiform editions and translations with edition and witness identifiers
archaeological excavation reports and scientific dating with stratigraphic context
local inscriptions with find context and explicit chronological limits
critically described Hebrew Bible textual witnesses and modern translations with composition and dependency cautions
licensed gazetteers and reviewed site-identification records
terrain, hydrography and routes that do not depict historical territories
catalog, holdings, copyright and lawful-access metadata for sealed held-out atlases

candidate_entities.label: Kingdom of Judah under Hezekiah
candidate_entities.status_rule: Local control requires a named-locality relation distinct from Assyrian conquest, siege, tribute, deportation or general royal title.

candidate_entities.label: Ekron under Padî and the 701 political crisis
candidate_entities.status_rule: Padî’s kingship, his detention, Assyrian restoration and tribute are recorded as separate relations; none alone proves continuous local administration outside named Ekron.

candidate_entities.label: Ashdod under Mitinti
candidate_entities.status_rule: Mitinti’s title and receipt of unnamed towns establish a political path but do not locate the transferred towns or their subsequent administration.

candidate_entities.label: Gaza under Ṣilli-Bēl
candidate_entities.status_rule: Ṣilli-Bēl’s title and receipt of unnamed towns establish a political path but do not locate the transferred towns or their subsequent administration.

candidate_entities.label: Ashkelon under Ṣidqâ
candidate_entities.status_rule: Cities explicitly called Ṣidqâ’s may support a local dynastic relation; Assyrian capture terminates or contests that relation without automatically creating Assyrian local administration.

contested_features.activation_rule: No campaign route, siege, conquest list or military presence may enter allocation without a separate supported local-administration claim.
The destruction horizon may constrain chronology and event location; it cannot define Judah’s extent or Assyrian local administration.

deviation_policy: Any post-freeze change requires a versioned amendment committed before affected analysis and reported beside the preregistered result. After held-out content is opened, changes to research inputs, model choices, candidate priority, units or denominator are post hoc and cannot replace the preregistered result.
expected_failure_modes: the 701 BCE horizon is presented as a day-level snapshot
Assyrian royal rhetoric is treated as neutral reporting
parallel royal inscriptions or translations are counted as independent lineages
conquest, siege, tribute, suzerainty, military presence and local administration are collapsed
unnamed transferred Judahite towns are assigned invented locations
Lachish destruction is converted directly into political control
late-eighth-century destruction layers are all assigned to 701
Hebrew Bible composition and literary relationships are ignored
ancient names are matched to modern sites without identification uncertainty
a sparse point set makes model defaults dominate
a binary allocation erases contested or unresolved localities
the held-out atlas expresses fewer than eight locked units
thumbnail, label or snippet leakage contaminates a comparator
automated checks are mistaken for proof of a person’s complete browsing history

held_out_evaluation.denominator_rule: Score every locked unit as aligned, not_aligned, not_expressed or not_comparable. Report aligned/(aligned+not_aligned) with all four counts; no unit may be removed after opening.
held_out_evaluation.interpretation_rule: Fewer than eight expressed comparable units makes the comparator inconclusive. Agreement is agreement with one publication under the frozen rubric, never historical accuracy.
held_out_evaluation.isolation_rule: The registered atlas remains metadata-only and outside sources, observations, claims, model decisions, scenarios and spatial inputs. Any search-result thumbnail, map-label or legend exposure contaminates and excludes that candidate.
held_out_evaluation.opening_gate: A second reconstructed_pre_evaluation Git commit must freeze the evidence state, scenario settings, code version, calibration, outputs, fixed place coordinates, evaluation rubric and hashes before first atlas-body access.

lineage_rules.claim: A claim lists supporting and challenging observations, BCE horizon applicability, named spatial referent, ontology layer and status. Archaeological destruction supports an event horizon only to its actual resolution.
lineage_rules.model_decision: Only a supported named-locality local-control claim may authorize a control point. Imperial relations, military events, transfers without named objects and unresolved identifications remain display context or exclusions.
lineage_rules.observation: One observation records one locatable statement or measurement. Conquest, siege, tribute, suzerainty, military presence, dynastic title, transfer and local administration are separate observation types.
lineage_rules.source: Every source records a stable locator, access scope, rights status, access date and source-lineage identifier. Editions or witnesses that repeat the Assyrian royal account remain one lineage unless demonstrated otherwise.

prior_information_disclosure: Before this freeze, the feasibility audit used only the twelve logged searches and ten logged text or catalog access attempts in feasibility-audit.json.
No historical territorial map body, plate, PDF map page, thumbnail intentionally selected for viewing, screenshot, OCR, vector or boundary derivative was opened, downloaded or parsed.

A search result for the Oxford Bible Atlas exposed a front-cover thumbnail, and unrelated search results exposed Bible-atlas map-label summaries. Those publications are excluded and recorded as contaminated.
ORACC witnesses Q003496 and Q003945 and any parallel translations are treated as one Assyrian royal-inscription lineage unless later source criticism demonstrates an independent tradition.
The Hebrew Bible path is prior information only at this stage; any later use must record textual layer, composition issues and possible literary or historical dependence.
prohibited_evidence: historical territorial map bodies, thumbnails, plates, screenshots, OCR, vectors or derivatives before the evaluation gate
search-result labels, legends or map summaries used as research evidence
Assyrian conquest, siege, tribute, suzerainty or military presence promoted directly to local administration
multiple Assyrian inscription copies or modern translations counted automatically as independent source lineages
Hebrew Bible passages treated as uncritical independent confirmation
destruction layers assigned to 701 solely because they are late eighth century
unnamed transferred towns converted into invented locality anchors
model defaults or calibration values presented as source evidence
research_question: During the 701 BCE horizon of Sennacherib’s third campaign and its directly reported political dispositions, which named localities in the Joppa–Ekron–Lachish–Jerusalem corridor can inscriptional, archaeological and non-territorial-map evidence support as local-control points, transfer objects, contested places or unresolved localities of Judah, Ekron, Ashdod, Gaza and Ashkelon, while keeping Assyrian conquest, tribute, suzerainty, military presence and local administration distinct?

spatial_scope.exclusion_rule: Exclude empire-wide extrapolation, unnamed captured or transferred towns as invented points, and any coordinate, boundary or label derived from an existing historical territorial map.
spatial_scope.inclusion_rule: Include the twelve locked named localities and only additional places with explicit 701 campaign/disposition relevance inside the box; modern coordinates require an identified gazetteer or archaeological-site record.
spatial_scope.name: Southern Levantine Joppa–Ekron–Lachish–Jerusalem corridor and adjacent Philistine centers

stop_conditions: Stop with NO_RECONSTRUCTION if the post-freeze budget is exhausted without the reconstruction gate.
Stop a gap after its success criterion is met or two targeted follow-ups add no admissible evidence.
Stop and record a protocol deviation if held-out map content is exposed before the second pre-evaluation freeze.
Do not alter evidence, parameters, candidate order, evaluation units or denominator in response to held-out results.

success_criteria.evaluation_gate: A lineage-bearing reconstruction and every locked evaluation input are frozen in a second Git commit before the primary comparator is opened; all outcomes, including an inconclusive comparator, are reported without tuning.
success_criteria.phase_one: A GO feasibility audit, strict frozen preregistration, metadata-only held-out register, non-reconstruction case skeleton, BCE chronology contract and passing isolation tests; no polygon is produced.
success_criteria.reconstruction_gate: At least two modeled entities each have two independent, legally accessible and horizon-applicable named-locality local-control relations; at least ten locatable spatial candidates derive from four independent source lineages; at least two counterevidence or exclusion relations are retained; every admitted source has a stable locator and rights record.

astronomical_year_numbering.usage_rule: Astronomical year −700 may be used only for computation. Public research records retain era=BCE and year_bce=701 and never serialize a negative ISO date.

temporal_scope.bridge_rule: Evidence is horizon-applicable only when it explicitly belongs to the third campaign or a directly reported disposition. Earlier and later texts or strata are context unless a reviewed continuity or synchronization argument is recorded.
temporal_scope.chronology_uncertainty: The campaign is conventionally assigned to 701 BCE, but individual operations, textual compositions, archaeological destructions and immediate dispositions are not uniformly month- or day-resolved; disputed synchronisms remain explicit.
temporal_scope.horizon_definition: The unit is the conventionally dated 701 BCE third-campaign sequence and the political dispositions directly reported as consequences of that campaign. It is neither a day-level snapshot nor a claim that every event was simultaneous.
prohibited_representations: day-precise snapshot inferred from year-level evidence
silent equivalence between textual composition date and narrated event date
